category_title: Highly anxious students with ASD characterized by pervasive sensory rituals and wariness
minimal_context: The student and teacher are in the school dinner hall attempting to play a simple throw and catch game with a ball.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's play a simple throw and catch game with this ball.

STUDENT: (Sits close to the teacher, holding hands and looking to the teacher for reassurance before briefly tossing the ball back.)

TUTOR: Here is the ball again. Throw it back.

STUDENT: (Watches the dog in order to move away if it gets too close, then becomes preoccupied with following markings on the floor in a repetitive manner.)

TUTOR: We are still playing. Come back and catch the ball.

STUDENT: (Moves further away from the dog and chooses to leave the room before the end of the session.)

options.A: Give the student stars, stickers, and applause as a reward for playing the ball game.
options.B: Put off the planned ball game and wait until the student returns to the room.
options.C: Suggest a turn-taking game with the ball to encourage the student to participate.
options.D: Joke a lot and laugh at oneself to encourage the student to play the game.
